chosen.title: Taming the Star: How AI Learned to Hold Fusion Plasma Together
chosen.rationale: In June 2026 the U.S. DOE launched STELLAR-AI (Princeton Plasma Physics Lab) and researchers are now handing second-by-second plasma control to AI fast enough to kill an instability before a human could register it — a genuine 2026 inflection for clean energy that sits exactly at Kenji's intersection of AI, clean energy, and physical mechanism-you-can-picture, with a built-in honest reckoning (private-sector hype vs. scientific verification).

sources.name: Forbes — Working On Fusion: AI Drives Energy Acceleration
World Economic Forum — How AI will help get fusion from lab to grid

rejected_candidates.title: One Brain, Many Bodies: The Race to Build a Foundation Model for Every Robot
rejected_candidates.rationale: 2026 is the year of the vision-language-action 'robot foundation model' — GEN-1 crossed a mastery threshold (99% success where prior models hit 64%) and startups like Physical Intelligence and Skild sell the brain, not the body; this is the mechanism story behind the humanoid headlines, distinct from AIMA's deployment/IPO and 'world model' pieces, and squarely Kenji's love of how the thing actually works.

rejected_candidates.title: Forecasting the Planet: How AI Weather Models Went Operational and Left the Supercomputers Behind
rejected_candidates.rationale: NOAA just deployed a full operational suite of AI-driven global weather models (fine-tuned from GraphCast), and foundation models like Microsoft's Aurora and NVIDIA's Earth-2/Atlas now match physics-based forecasts in seconds of GPU inference instead of hours — a watershed for climate resilience and disaster warning that fits Kenji's climate-tech beat and his gift for making scale feel like wonder.
